svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Why carbon makes so many compounds."], [1, "Carbon forms four covalent bonds: methane has them arranged as a tetrahedron."], [4, "Carbons join into chains, like butane..."], [6, "...branched chains..."], [8, "...rings..."], [10, "...and double bonds."], [12, "So a huge variety of stable molecules is possible: the basis of life."]]
svg.title: Carbon compounds
svg.desc: Carbon forms four covalent bonds: methane with tetrahedral bonds, butane as a straight chain, methylpropane as a branched chain, cyclohexane as a ring and ethene with a double bond.
svg.text: Structural formulas; grey = carbon, white = hydrogen.

g.data-info: Carbon has 4 electrons in its outer shell, so it forms 4 covalent bonds.
Four single bonds point to the corners of a tetrahedron, 109.5° apart.
Carbon atoms bond to each other in chains of any length.
Same formula as butane, different arrangement (an isomer).
Carbon chains can close into rings, as in glucose and steroids.
Two carbons can share two pairs of electrons (C=C).
